newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close at new 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close at new 1996 high.

text.p: Rallies in oil giant YPF and the heavyweight telephone stocks fuelled a winning streak on the Argentine bolsa Thursday, pushing blue chips to their third consecutive record close for 1996.
Traders said the upward momentum could linger Friday.

"The market is very firm and had surprisingly strong volume today considering there's a general strike," said Miguel Daneri of Boston Securities, referring to a 24-hour trade union protest against government labor reforms.
The MerVal index jumped 1.2 percent to a year's high of 650.04, boosting gains this week to 3.6 percent.

"The MerVal managed to close a notch above the psychological barrier of 650, which is a very good sign," said an analyst at a large Argentine bank. "However, if it stalls slightly above these levels tomorrow we could be facing a downward correction early next week."
Traders said the bolsa mirrored strength in the fixed income market, which continued climbing on rumors of a hefty government bond issue likely to be announced in January.
"Talk of the bond issue is giving the markets a lift, and stocks are also already anticipating economic indicators for the first half of next year," said Daneri.
The bolsa's broad market index rose 1.3 percent in the session, with winners pounding losers 43 to 10 and 14 issues closing flat.
Floor volume totaled 21.9 million pesos, compared to 23 million Monday and a token 6.3 million pesos traded Tuesday when the session ended three hours early.

Among main-tier stocks, market bellwether YPF gained 1.0 percent while heavily traded Telecom and Telefonica rose 2.5 percent and 2.3 percent each. Top gainers were petrochemical concern Ipako, steelmaker Acindar and Bansud bank, which surged 4.7 percent, 3.7 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal losers were petrochemical concern Indupa and Banco Frances, which shed 0.6 percent and 0.5 percent each.
